headline: Light showers overnight into Monday morning give way to a dry, warming week, but the big story is the coast: record-breaking King Tides plus a building swell bring major, locally extreme coastal flooding to the Orange and San Diego County beaches Tuesday through Friday, while Thanksgiving and Friday run 5 to 15 degrees warmer than normal with likely weak Santa Ana winds.

sections.title: Today & Tonight
sections.text: Clouds thicken over the coast and valleys Sunday night as a weakening disturbance moves through, bringing isolated to scattered light showers to the coast and valleys through about 2 AM, and lingering in San Diego County, including coastal Carlsbad, until about 10 AM Monday. Rain falls at 0.10 inch per hour or less, and totals stay at 0.20 inch or less. The mountains could see a dusting of snow above about 6,000–6,500 feet. Highs are expected to be similar to the day before.

sections.title: Short Term
sections.text: Clouds thin out Monday and clear by Monday evening, leaving only high, thin clouds Monday night into Tuesday. A brief, weak build of high pressure brings a few degrees of warming, and Tuesday is warm and dry. A weak disturbance crosses California Wednesday, but the forecast keeps trending dry, with only a small change in temperatures between Tuesday and Wednesday at the coast and in the valleys.

sections.title: Long Term
sections.text: Thanksgiving Thursday and Friday turn warmer and drier as high pressure sits over California and winds blow offshore (from the land toward the sea), with highs 5 to 15 degrees above average. Friday looks warmest, with a 70–90 percent chance of 80 degrees or higher across the coast, valleys and lower deserts, but no chance of 90 at this time. One high-detail wind model gives a 60–75 percent chance of a weak Santa Ana wind event and a 25–30 percent chance of weak-to-moderate Santa Ana winds; stronger winds are most likely if a low-pressure system to our east sets up over northern Mexico, which only about 18 percent of model runs show. By Saturday an approaching storm system likely pushes the high pressure east, bringing gradual cooling Saturday into next Sunday and slight chances of rain as early as Sunday; about 60 percent of model runs bring that system into Northern California, the scenario most likely to give Southern California light rain.

coast: Coastal flooding is the main hazard this week for the Orange County and San Diego County coasts. Morning high tides are climbing (7.35 feet at La Jolla Sunday), with the highest tides Tuesday through Thursday and the King Tides peaking Wednesday; morning high tides of 7.9–8.3 feet are expected Tuesday through Thursday, about 1.1–1.2 feet above normal tide predictions, which will likely break the all-time tide records set in late October. Surf stays around 3–5 feet through Wednesday afternoon, then a large west swell sharply raises it late Wednesday into Thursday, with 6–8 foot breakers Thursday and sets of 10 feet or more on west-facing beaches, easing Friday but still elevated at 5–8 feet. A Coastal Flood Advisory (moderate to locally major flooding) runs until 4 AM Tuesday, followed by a Coastal Flood Warning from 4 AM Tuesday to 1 PM Friday, with major coastal flooding expected and locally extreme flooding Thursday. For boaters, no marine hazards are expected through Tuesday; Wednesday afternoon into Thursday brings seas of 8–12 feet, locally up to 14 feet in the outer waters, plus northwest winds of about 23–29 mph (20–25 knots) near San Clemente Island Wednesday afternoon and evening, hazardous for small craft, with seas lowering Thursday afternoon.
watch_for: Major, locally extreme coastal flooding: Coastal Flood Advisory until 4 AM Tuesday, then a Coastal Flood Warning from 4 AM Tuesday to 1 PM Friday, worst Thursday with record tides and big surf.
How strong Thursday–Friday's offshore winds get (60–75% chance of weak Santa Ana winds, 25–30% chance of weak-to-moderate) and how warm Friday turns out.
Whether next weekend's storm system brings any light rain by Sunday.
confidence: Forecasters are confident in tonight's light showers, a dry Tuesday–Wednesday, and warmer, drier weather Thursday–Friday, but less sure how strong the Santa Ana winds get and have low confidence in the details of possible rain early next week.
